narrative:
I set out to kill this and I got closer than I expected on almost every axis except the one the spec itself named as its highest-value unknown.

The good news first, because it is real and it is the reason the opportunity does not die outright. The spec says Nike's federation rights at Doha 2027 'could not be confirmed' and calls that the single most valuable unknown. It resolves in the opportunity's favour: FIBA signed an eleven-year strategic partnership with Nike making Nike the official FIBA product partner across apparel, footwear and equipment for its senior men's, women's and youth flagship national-team competitions, explicitly naming the FIBA Basketball World Cups of 2019, 2023 and 2027 (insidethegames.biz / basketball.ca / weartesters, checked 3 Sep 2026). Doha 2027 is inside Nike's existing rights. That single fact is worth more than everything else in this spec.

And it immediately inverts the spec's own sequencing logic. That agreement runs 2017-2027 and I could find no renewal or extension announcement anywhere. So Nike's FIBA rights cover DOHA - and lapse before the LA28 cycle, before the 2029 U19 cycle and before the 2031 World Cup the TRANSIT chassis was explicitly designed to survive into. Worse for the LA leg: FIBA signed the Swiss brand FOURTEEN as official apparel supplier for ALL its 3x3 global events from the 2026 season (fiba3x3.com, sportcal, checked 3 Sep 2026), so the 3x3 platform the spec makes its hero use-case is not Nike's platform. And at LA28 itself, Fanatics holds the LA28 and Team USA merchandise, licensing and retail agreement including physical retail at the venues, Ralph Lauren is an Official Outfitter of the LA28 Games, and Nike's Team USA role is on-field gear (sportspro, frontofficesports, la28.org, checked 3 Sep 2026). The programme is therefore strongest exactly where the spec treats it as a pilot, and weakest exactly where the spec treats it as the payoff. DOHA is not a rehearsal for VALLEY; DOHA is a closing rights window and VALLEY is somebody else's licence.

The hardest hit is to the mechanism. The whole why-now rests on A04-S3 - adidas apparel +35% currency-neutral on World Cup kit demand - read as proof that a dated moment pulls full-price apparel volume. Nike has already run that experiment at the largest possible scale and lost. Going into the Paris 2024 quarter Nike guided sales down about 10%, which coverage identified as the first Olympic-quarter sales decline since at least the 2000 Sydney Games, against an average +9.9% in prior Olympic quarters - and it happened while Nike put Olympic product into more than 8,000 retail doors worldwide (cnbc.com 27 Jun 2024, sherwood.news, checked 3 Sep 2026). The spec's own contradictory-evidence section concedes adidas' lift was bought with EUR 212M of extra marketing and rests on kit rights adidas owns. Combine the two and the honest statement of the mechanism is not 'a date pulls full price'; it is 'owning the kit of the teams people are watching pulls full price, and Nike has that at Doha 2027 and not at LA28.'

The product is less new than it reads. Nike introduced Aero-FIT to basketball on 17 July 2026 with the Sabrina 4 collection - a jersey AND shorts, with open and closed mesh zones, listed at USD 75 (about.nike.com, nike.com, checked 3 Sep 2026; this also corroborates the A03-S4 price the auditor flagged as possibly an echo). The right-to-win line that Nike 'simply has not routed [Aero-FIT] to basketball shorts' is no longer true. On the SESSION short's two headline features, the auditor already verified that Nike's DNA 6-inch UV Woven (FN2659) ships UVA/UVB protection, side pockets, a zippered utility pocket sized to hold a phone, and a woven face marketed for abrasion. What is left is thigh coverage and pocket placement - real, incremental, and not a programme.

On novelty of the idea itself, both the external and the internal answers are unflattering. Externally, Mitchell & Ness has already launched an LA28 collection through Fanatics as an official LA28 licensee, and an LA28 x NBA All-Star Mitchell & Ness Swingman Mesh Short is already listed at retail - a Games-marked basketball short in market roughly two years before the Games, against a proposed STAND at USD 85 that would carry no Games marks (la28.org, fanatics.ca listing, checked 3 Sep 2026). Internally, Jordan Brand has run an annual dated, place-anchored streetball capsule - Quai 54 - for years, with the 2026 edition including full basketball kits, jerseys and shorts, released in July in Paris (sneakernews, houseofheat, checked 3 Sep 2026). The spec's claim that 'nobody owns the join between a PLM season calendar and a federation qualification calendar' may be true of the FIBA calendar specifically, but the moment-anchored shorts capsule as a mechanism is something Nike Inc. ships every year, and the spec lists Quai 54 as one of its own lead markets without noticing it is already occupied by a sister brand.

On price, the one clean anchor the spec found cuts against it on inspection. Its own comparable - the Nike USMNT 2026 Home Stadium Replica Short at USD 55 - is showing at USD 44.00 with code, and the away version at USD 34.99, on Fanatics in the launch year of a home World Cup (fanatics.com search-result summaries, checked 3 Sep 2026). That is Nike's most directly analogous event-linked federation BOTTOM, at the exact moment the mechanism is supposed to be working, discounting. The claim that a date holds full price is not supported by the closest available observation of a Nike dated bottom.

On size, Doha gets smaller the closer you look. Qatar's entire sports market is put at about USD 955M in 2024 across all sports (imarcgroup, checked 3 Sep 2026), and the visible community basketball activity is substantially expat-driven - the Pinoy Basketball Qatar league is running its 37th Rising Basketball League season - which points the DOHA drop straight at the consumer whose price band A03-S10 puts under PHP 3,000 (~USD 52), well below the SESSION price. The base's own admission that it has essentially zero Gulf evidence is not a gap that a good brief closes; it is the market the first drop is scheduled into.

Finally, the portfolio problem, which is the one a PLM will actually act on. Strip the date and the cartography and OPP-06 is three product ideas the same synthesis already funds separately: COURT is OPP-01 Like-Colored (the colour-matched short-plus-compression set built on A06-S3), SESSION is OPP-02 Found Outdoors (UPF, storage, hot-market outdoor play, the identical consumer description), STAND is OPP-07 The Other Half and OPP-08 Full Range (fan bottoms, wide and long, event doors). Its unique content is a graphic direction and a calendar. That is a marketing calendar item, not a third of a line plan.

What survives, and I want to be precise about it: a single FA27 DOHA activation, executed on an existing chassis, inside Nike's existing FIBA rights, sized as a marketing vehicle with a merchandising floor - which is exactly what the spec's own honest-sizing paragraph says it is. What does not survive is the two-drop TRANSIT programme, the SS28 VALLEY leg as specified, the USD 55/70/85 ladder as a full-price architecture, the event-retail channel line, and the claim that this is a new opportunity rather than a launch window for opportunities already on the board. The spec is unusually honest - it flags most of these itself - but the honesty is in the footnotes and the score is in the headline, and 57 prices the headline.

kill_attempts.angle: The mechanism does not transfer to Nike: Nike already ran the largest dated-moment apparel play available to it and posted its worst Olympic quarter on record
kill_attempts.argument: The entire why-now is A04-S3 read as 'a dated moment pulls full-price apparel volume through a promotional floor.' But Nike itself is the control experiment. Going into the Paris 2024 Olympic quarter Nike guided revenue down about 10%, described in coverage as the first Olympic-quarter sales decline since at least the 2000 Sydney Games against an average +9.9% lift in prior Olympic quarters - and that happened while Nike shipped Olympic product into more than 8,000 retail doors worldwide. adidas' +35% is not evidence that dates sell apparel; it is evidence that owning the kit of the teams people are watching sells apparel, and the spec's own contradictory-evidence section concedes the lift came with EUR 212M of incremental World Cup marketing. A moment without owned kit rights and without matching marketing spend is not the adidas mechanism, it is a graphics story.
kill_attempts.evidence: cnbc.com 27 Jun 2024 (Nike Q4 FY24 / Q1 FY25 guidance, ~-10%, 8,000+ doors) and sherwood.news 'Even the 2024 Paris Olympics can't save Nike' (Olympic-quarter average +9.9% vs 7.9% non-Olympic), both checked 3 Sep 2026; A04-S3 (VERIFIED); adidas press release 30 Jul 2026 cited in the spec (EUR 212M higher marketing).

kill_attempts.angle: Rights, part 1 - the highest-value unknown resolves FOR the opportunity, but only for the half the spec calls the pilot
kill_attempts.argument: I tried to kill this on rights and the attack failed for Doha. FIBA and Nike signed an eleven-year strategic partnership making Nike the official FIBA product partner across apparel, footwear and equipment for FIBA's senior men's, women's and youth flagship national-team competitions, with the FIBA Basketball World Cups of 2019, 2023 and 2027 named explicitly. The spec's stated top unknown - 'whether Nike is a federation kit supplier for any team at the FIBA World Cup Qatar 2027' - is answered: Nike holds the property-level product partnership covering the event. This is the single strongest fact anyone has added to this opportunity and it should raise, not lower, the DOHA leg.
kill_attempts.evidence: insidethegames.biz 'FIBA signs 11-year strategic partnership with Nike'; basketball.ca and weartesters coverage of the same announcement; search-verified 3 Sep 2026 (host pages egress-blocked, terms reproduced consistently across three independent outlets). Note the base contains no such signal - this is new evidence, not a digest id.

kill_attempts.angle: Rights, part 2 - the same deal expires in 2027, FIBA 3x3 apparel belongs to another brand, and LA28 fan retail belongs to Fanatics; the chassis argument inverts
kill_attempts.argument: The Nike-FIBA agreement runs 2017-2027 and I found no renewal or extension announcement. So the rights cover DOHA and lapse before the LA28 cycle, the 2029 U19 cycle and the 2031 World Cup - precisely the horizon the TRANSIT chassis was invented to survive into. Separately, FIBA signed Swiss brand FOURTEEN as official apparel supplier for ALL FIBA 3x3 global events from the 2026 season, so the 3x3 competition platform the spec makes its hero use-case is not Nike's. At LA28, Fanatics holds the LA28 and Team USA merchandise, licensing and retail agreement including physical retail across LA28 venues, Ralph Lauren is an Official Outfitter of the Games, and Nike's Team USA role is on-field gear. The spec's central sequencing argument - DOHA as a cheap pilot for the real SS28 VALLEY buy - is therefore backwards: DOHA is a closing rights window that must be used, VALLEY is a licence Nike does not hold.
kill_attempts.evidence: insidethegames.biz (term 2017-2027, no renewal found); fiba3x3.com and fiba.basketball 'FIBA signs innovative global apparel partnership with FOURTEEN for 3x3 Basketball' plus sportcal, launching 2026 season; sportspro.com and frontofficesports.com on the Fanatics LA28/Team USA merchandising, licensing and venue retail deal; la28.org newsroom on Ralph Lauren as Official Outfitter. All checked 3 Sep 2026. Contrast with the spec's ~20% event/in-arena channel allocation.

kill_attempts.angle: The event channel is not Nike's to sell into - FIBA appoints a global master licensee and LA28 retail is Fanatics
kill_attempts.argument: The distribution plan allocates roughly 20% of the mix to event and in-arena retail at the four Doha venues, the Doha fan zones and the LA28 3x3 and fan sites, justified by A05-S7 (full price holds at events). But event merchandise at a FIBA World Cup is a licensed programme: FIBA appointed IMG as global master licensee for the 2023 World Cup, with product sold on-site at all five venues, at official fan shops and retailers in the host countries and via the official online store. At LA28, Fanatics operates the physical retail across venues. So the 20% line is not a Nike channel decision; it is a licence Nike would have to buy, on terms nobody in this analysis has priced, and probably as one licensee among many rather than as the destination brand. A05-S7's full-price observation was made at an Unrivaled game where the league controls its own merchandise - not a transferable read.

Against A05-S7 (VERIFIED) and the spec's channel mix.

kill_attempts.angle: It is not new externally - a Games-marked basketball short is already in market two years early, with real marks the Nike capsule would not have
kill_attempts.argument: STAND 11 in. at USD 85 is proposed as the fan-zone and in-arena bottom. Mitchell & Ness has already launched an official LA28 collection through its Fanatics relationship as an LA28 licensee, and an LA28 x NBA All-Star Mitchell & Ness Swingman Mesh Short is already listed at retail. So the exact occasion - a Games-marked basketball short for the fan who owns the top - is occupied, by the incumbent the spec already names as its competitive risk (A05-S3, A02-S5), carrying licensed marks, roughly two years before the Games. A Nike STAND short with court-line cartography and no Games or federation marks is the weaker product at a similar price, and the spec's own contradictory evidence already rates STAND the weakest-evidenced of the three styles (audit contradiction 14, A05-S4).

kill_attempts.angle: It is not new internally - Nike Inc. already runs a dated, place-anchored streetball shorts capsule every year, and the spec lists it as a lead market without noticing
kill_attempts.argument: The claim that 'nobody owns the join between a PLM season calendar and a federation qualification calendar' is used to argue the window is open. But the mechanism - a dated, place-named, culturally-anchored basketball capsule with shorts in it - is something Nike Inc. ships annually as Jordan Brand's Quai 54, whose 2026 edition released in July with full basketball kits, jerseys, shorts, tees and outerwear tied to the Paris tournament. The spec then names 'France around Quai 54 at Roland-Garros in July' as one of TRANSIT's lead markets, which means the programme's own launch plan collides with a sister brand's established annual property. Whatever is genuinely unowned here is narrower than the spec claims: it is the FIBA qualification calendar specifically, not moment-anchored shorts.

kill_attempts.angle: The product differentiation is already shipped - Aero-FIT is on a basketball short today, and Nike's UV woven short already carries UPF plus a phone-sized zip pocket
kill_attempts.argument: Right-to-win asset (2) says Nike's cooling platform 'debuted on 2026 federation football kits' and Nike 'simply has not routed it to basketball shorts.' That was true when the specialist files were written and is not true now: Nike introduced Aero-FIT to basketball on 17 July 2026 with the Sabrina 4 signature collection - jersey and shorts, open and closed mesh zones - and the Aero-FIT basketball short is listed at USD 75. Separately, the auditor verified directly that Nike's DNA 6-inch UV Woven (FN2659) already ships UVA/UVB protection, side pockets, a zippered utility pocket sized to hold a phone, and a woven abrasion face. kill_attempts.angle: Price - Nike's own event-linked federation bottom is already discounting in the launch year of the moment it was made for
kill_attempts.argument: The spec anchors COURT at USD 55 on the Nike USMNT 2026 Home Stadium Replica Short. That short is showing at USD 44.00 with code, and the away version at USD 34.99, in 2026 - the year of a home World Cup, at the peak of exactly the mechanism the programme is built on. If a dated federation bottom with real national-team marks cannot hold USD 55 during its own World Cup, the proposition that an unlicensed USD 70 SESSION and a USD 85 STAND will hold full price on a basketball moment is not supported by the closest available observation. Layer on the auditor's verdict that three mutually incompatible Nike ladders exist in the base with none from a retrieved page, and A02-S4's finding that USD 78-90 premium basketball shorts clear only at 40-50% off, and the ladder has to be treated as aspiration.

kill_attempts.angle: Consumer need - the base shows fans buy tops at moments, and the spec concedes there is no observation of anyone buying shorts at one
kill_attempts.argument: The JTBD is asserted, not evidenced, and the spec says so: A01 contributes execution constraints only and 'NO evidence that any consumer buys basketball shorts around a national-team moment.' The strongest fan-fashion term in the base is 'female jersey outfit' at +494%, which argues for tops (A05-S4, and the auditor's explicit warning against the shorts inference). Nike's own Paris 2024 basketball fan headline was a USD 149.99 replica JERSEY sold through Fanatics, the Team USA Shop and the NBA Store; the bottoms were the accessory, and they are the ones now discounting. My own search for any shirt-versus-shorts attach data in football - the analogue sport, the mechanism being copied - returned nothing quantitative in either direction, only the historical note that kits used to be sold as shirt-plus-shorts units and that modern club and federation economics are described in terms of shirt sales. The demand assumption under the whole programme remains unmeasured.

kill_attempts.angle: Geography - the first drop is scheduled into the market with zero evidence, a small total sports economy, and a consumer whose price band is half the hero price

Qatar's entire sports market - all sports, all categories - is put at about USD 955M in 2024. The visible community basketball activity is substantially expatriate: the Pinoy Basketball Qatar league is running its 37th Rising Basketball League season, which points the DOHA drop at the Filipino consumer whose price band A03-S10 puts under PHP 3,000 (~USD 52), against a SESSION hero at USD 70 that the spec's own regional notes already say is out of band for the Philippines. SESSION 9 in. as a UPF, storage-engineered outdoor short for hot markets is OPP-02 Found Outdoors, whose target-consumer line in the synthesis is nearly word-for-word the same population. kill_attempts.angle: Execution - the gate that is the programme's 'best feature' may not have time to close, and the wholesale figure underneath it is contradicted inside the base
kill_attempts.argument: The central sequencing claim is that DOHA gives 'roughly eleven months' of read before the SS28 VALLEY buy commits. Check the arithmetic: DOHA is on shelf Jul-Sep 2027, the event runs 27 Aug - 12 Sep 2027, so a week-8 full-price sell-through read arrives around Oct-Nov 2027. A SS28 delivery landing for a Jul 2028 Games has to be bought into wholesale order books in roughly the same window. Eleven months would put the SS28 commit in the second half of 2028 - after the Games. So the gate is at best a few weeks wide and quite possibly zero, which makes it ceremonial in exactly the way the spec says it must not be. Separately the base cannot agree on the channel the plan is routed to: A04-S1 says Nike wholesale grew 6% reported while A02-S7 says wholesale grew 4% in Q4 and full-year FY26 - the spec quotes ~6% without reconciling it. And the team-dealer pool (A04-S9) is described as having less certain 2026 visibility after tariff-driven pull-forward, which is the pool the COURT set depends on.

strongest_counterargument: "We already ran this play, at a bigger moment, and it didn't work. Nike put Paris 2024 product into more than 8,000 doors and posted its first Olympic-quarter sales decline since at least Sydney 2000. adidas' +35% isn't a lesson about dates - it's a lesson about owning the kit of the teams people are watching, plus EUR 212M of extra marketing. Now look at what we actually own at these two moments: we hold the FIBA product partnership through 2027, which covers Doha - so if you want to sell me something, sell me Doha, this year, on a chassis we already have. But at LA28, Fanatics owns the merchandise, licensing and venue retail, Ralph Lauren is the Official Outfitter, Mitchell & Ness already has LA28 shorts at retail with real marks, and FIBA's 3x3 apparel supplier is a Swiss brand called FOURTEEN. And when I strip the date out, COURT is Like-Colored, SESSION is Found Outdoors, STAND is The Other Half - three opportunities I'm already being asked to fund. So what you've brought me isn't a shorts programme. It's a launch window for opportunities that are already on the board, priced above a Nike Aero-FIT basketball short that shipped last July, against a USMNT replica short of our own that's already at USD 44 with code in the middle of a World Cup year."
adjustment_rationale:
Down from 57 to 39. One thing moved it up and six moved it down.

UP: the spec's own highest-value unknown resolved in its favour. Nike is FIBA's official product partner across apparel, footwear and equipment for flagship national-team competitions with the 2027 World Cup named, so DOHA sits inside existing rights. On its own this is worth roughly +8 to the Doha leg, and the spec correctly said it would move the score toward 70 on that confirmation.

DOWN, and heavier: (1) The mechanism has a Nike-specific disconfirmation the spec never looked for - Paris 2024 was Nike's worst Olympic quarter on record with product in 8,000+ doors, which converts 'a dated moment pulls full price' from a proven mechanism into a rights-and-marketing-dependent one. (2) The same FIBA agreement expires in 2027 with no renewal found, so the chassis-survives-to-2031 argument fails and the sequencing inverts: DOHA is a closing window, not a pilot for a bigger VALLEY. (3) LA28 fan merchandise, licensing and venue retail belong to Fanatics, Ralph Lauren is Official Outfitter, and FIBA 3x3 apparel belongs to FOURTEEN from 2026 - so the VALLEY leg, the 3x3 hero framing and ~20% of the channel mix are all rights Nike does not hold. (4) The fan-bottom occasion is already filled with licensed LA28 Mitchell & Ness swingman shorts, two years early. (5) The product differentiation is thinner than claimed: Aero-FIT already ships on a basketball short at USD 75 and Nike's DNA 6" UV Woven already carries UPF plus a phone-sized zip pocket, leaving thigh coverage and pocket placement. (6) The price architecture's own anchor is discounting in its moment year (USMNT replica short USD 55 to USD 44 with code). (7) Portfolio duplication: strip the date and this is OPP-01 + OPP-02 + OPP-07/08.

39 is a deliberate placement: too high to reject, because the DOHA rights window is real, time-limited, and cheap to test, and because a moment-linked full-price story is genuinely scarce in a flat-unit business (A03-S9). Too low to rank as a top opportunity, because the programme as specified spends its energy on the half of the calendar Nike does not own and duplicates product ideas that are already funded. It would move to about 55 if a merchant confirms wholesale appetite for a non-replenishable FA27 capsule AND Nike Team Sports confirms a licensing route to Doha event retail. It would move to about 25 if internal history shows the Paris 2024 or 2023 World Cup basketball capsules cleared at markdown.
adjusted_verdict_note: Survives DEMOTED and RESCOPED, not as specified. What survives: a single FA27 DOHA activation, executed inside Nike's existing FIBA product partnership before it expires in 2027, on an existing chassis (the Aero-FIT or DNA basketball short), sized as a marketing vehicle with a merchandising floor - which is what the spec's own honest-sizing paragraph already concedes it is. What does NOT survive: the two-drop TRANSIT programme as a standalone line-plan opportunity; the SS28 VALLEY leg as specified (rights held by Fanatics/Ralph Lauren/LA28 licensees, 3x3 apparel by FOURTEEN); the ~20% event and in-arena retail channel (FIBA master licensee; Fanatics at LA28); the USD 55/70/85 ladder as a full-price architecture; STAND 11 in. at USD 85 against licensed LA28 Mitchell & Ness swingman shorts already in market; and the claim that this is a NEW opportunity rather than a launch window for OPP-01, OPP-02 and OPP-07/08.

validation_plan.question: What exactly do Nike's FIBA rights permit at the 2027 World Cup - national-team uniform supply, replica/fan product, event-site retail, use of event marks - and does the agreement extend past 2027 into the 2029 U19 and 2031 World Cup cycles? If not, is renewal in negotiation?
validation_plan.method: Pull the FIBA partnership contract and term sheet from Nike Sports Marketing / Legal; one call with the FIBA account lead. Ask specifically whether the 3x3 carve-out to FOURTEEN (from the 2026 season) limits anything Nike can sell around 3x3, and what IMG-style master-licensee terms would apply to Doha venue and fan-zone retail.
validation_plan.who: Nike Sports Marketing (FIBA account) + Legal/Licensing, with Basketball Apparel PLM in the room
validation_plan.cost_time: Zero external cost; 1-2 weeks. This is the single highest-value validation and it is entirely internal - it should happen before any further work on this opportunity.

validation_plan.question: How did Nike's last three event-linked basketball apparel capsules actually perform - Paris 2024 Team USA, the 2023 FIBA World Cup, and the Quai 54 series - by full-price sell-through at week 8, markdown depth, and shorts-versus-tops mix?
validation_plan.method: Internal sell-through pull from Nike Merchandising/Demand & Supply, split by silhouette. The decisive cut is BOTTOMS as a share of capsule units and their full-price rate versus the capsule's tops. This is the direct test of the JTBD, and Nike has the data.
validation_plan.who: Nike Merchandising Analytics + Jordan Brand (for Quai 54) + Team Sports
validation_plan.cost_time: Zero external cost; 2-3 weeks. If bottoms cleared at markdown in all three, kill the opportunity.

validation_plan.question: Will wholesale partners actually book a non-replenishable, hard-expiry dated capsule in three inseams, and at what price and depth?
validation_plan.method: Structured buyer interviews with 6-8 accounts across the named doors - Dick's, Foot Locker, JD, KICKZ, Rebel (AU), Titan 22 (PH) - presenting the FA27 DOHA concept board with the three price points. Ask for indicative units and the price at which they would take it without markdown support. Run it as a pre-line concept review, not a survey.
validation_plan.who: Nike Wholesale/Key Accounts sales leads, briefed by PLM
validation_plan.cost_time: Low cost (travel/time only); 4-6 weeks. Must complete before any FA27 development spend.

validation_plan.question: Do consumers in the target cohort actually buy a SHORT at a national-team moment, or only a top - and at what price?
validation_plan.method: Quantitative concept and price test (Gabor-Granger or van Westendorp) with n=1,200 across the US, Australia, the Philippines and Japan, plus a Qatar/UAE booster of n=300 to close the Gulf gap the auditor flagged. Test three things: purchase intent for a moment-linked short with marks versus without; the shorts-versus-jersey trade-off at a fixed budget; and price sensitivity at USD 55/70/85 against a Mitchell & Ness LA28 swingman short and a Nike Aero-FIT short at USD 75.
validation_plan.who: Nike Consumer Insights / external agency (Kantar, Savanta or equivalent)
validation_plan.cost_time: USD 80-140K; 6-8 weeks fielding plus 2 weeks analysis.

validation_plan.question: Is the SS28 VALLEY gate arithmetically real? When does the SS28 buy actually have to commit relative to a week-8 full-price read on the FA27 DOHA drop?
validation_plan.method: Map the actual FA27 and SS28 GTM calendars - line review, sample, showroom, booking close, factory commit - against the Doha event window (27 Aug - 12 Sep 2027) and a week-8 sell-through date. Get the real booking-close dates from Demand & Supply Management rather than assuming eleven months.
validation_plan.who: Nike Basketball Apparel PLM + Demand & Supply Management
validation_plan.cost_time: Zero cost; 3-5 days. If the gate is under 4 weeks wide, the spec's central sequencing argument fails and the opportunity should be re-underwritten as a one-drop DOHA activation.

validation_plan.question: Can full-thigh UPF 40-50 in a woven/knit hybrid, plus a bonded internal zip pocket and the trapped-sweat acceptance criteria, be delivered at a landed cost supporting USD 70 - and does it beat the shipping Aero-FIT basketball short on a wear test?
validation_plan.method: Costed tech-pack feasibility with two Tier-1 vendors, plus a 30-athlete outdoor wear test on asphalt at 30 C+ measuring the spec's own criteria (wet-weight gain at 45 min, dry-back time, saturated drawcord slip, wet cling) with the Nike Aero-FIT basketball short and the DNA 6 in. UV Woven as controls. The control comparison is the point: the claim only holds if it beats what Nike already ships.
validation_plan.who: Nike Apparel Innovation / Materials + Sport Research Lab; vendor costing via Sourcing
validation_plan.cost_time: USD 40-70K; 8-10 weeks including the wear test. Sequence after the rights answer, not before.

validation_plan.question: Does this programme add anything to the SS28 line that OPP-01, OPP-02 and OPP-07/08 do not already deliver?
validation_plan.method: Side-by-side line-architecture review putting the four specs on one wall, mapping SKU, silhouette, inseam, consumer, door and price. Force an explicit decision: fund the products separately and treat 'Doha to LA' as a marketing calendar and colour-up story on top of them, or fund it as a programme and cut the overlapping opportunities.
validation_plan.who: Basketball Apparel PLM leadership with Merchandising and Brand Marketing
validation_plan.cost_time: Zero cost; one half-day session. Should happen before portfolio ranking, because the current set double-counts the same product content three times.
